item_033.one_line_why: RDKit confirms identical 32-heavy-atom molecules; the discussed nitrile-to-OH replacement is absent, and no protein contact is claimed.

item_034.one_line_why: Cl-to-Br is the sole edit, but no halogen row is supplied: CYS95 contacts belong to C01/C02 and LEU168 to C04/C19/N03; ownership of the proposed halogen packing gains cannot be settled.

item_035.one_line_why: F-to-Cl is correct, but F01 faces SER345.C at 2.94 A; PHE233.CZ belongs to C10-C12 and VAL329.CG2 to C09/N08/O24, so retained-group contacts are assigned to the halogen.

item_036.one_line_why: Aryl Cl becomes CH(Cl)CH3, adding two carbons and an unspecified stereocentre rather than replacing C5 with methyl; the exact C5 mapping is unresolved and its uncertain LYS12 row cannot establish relief.

item_037.one_line_why: The 40-heavy-atom proposal is identical to the input, including its sulfonamide; the rationale never identifies an implemented edit or claims a protein contact.

item_038.one_line_why: The 32-heavy-atom structures and cyclopropane stereochemistry are identical; no edit occurs, and the asserted sulfonate is actually a sulfone with direct carbon-sulfur bonds.

item_039.one_line_why: Aryl Cl becomes CH(Cl)CH3, retaining every input carbon and adding an unspecified stereocentre; exact C5 ownership in the SMILES is unresolved, and the uncertain C5-LYS12 row does not support the claimed methyl replacement or relief.

item_040.one_line_why: The sole edit is aryl F-to-OH with all rings retained; increased polarity and general hydrogen-bonding capacity are sound, and no new measured pocket interaction is asserted.

item_041.one_line_why: Br-to-Cl is correct and the R centre is preserved; BR1 owns the uncertain SER14.O row, whereas LYS12 rows belong to retained C/O atoms, so a favorable halogen interaction with LYS12 is unsupported.

item_042.one_line_why: The actual edit adds phenolic OH; C1-CYS166.SG is a real 1.81 A covalent link, but the proposal neither replaces protein sulfur with water nor demonstrates disruption of that link.

item_043.one_line_why: The ester remains while the enol chain loses one carbon and becomes an oxime; GLU31/HIS34 packing belongs to retained C11-C17, and exact metal-oxygen ownership is unresolved, so maintained MN coordination is unsupported.

item_044.one_line_why: F16 owns the 3.37 A LEU191.CD1 contact and is removed, but the edit replaces full CF3 with isopropyl, losing all three fluorines and adding two carbons, rather than replacing one fluorine with methyl; R stereochemistry is retained.

item_045.one_line_why: The same 61-heavy-atom molecule and stereochemistry retain naphthyl; the suggested phenyl replacement is absent and would not add hydrogen-bonding capacity; no specific table contact is claimed.

item_046.one_line_why: The acrylamide carbonyl unit is deleted to give a hydrolytically labile N-vinylarylamine, not C=O-to-C-NH replacement; GLU167/ASP164 contacts belong to N01/N2 with unresolved exact mapping, and the asserted acceptor cannot hydrogen-bond to acid oxygens as claimed.

item_047.one_line_why: F-to-Cl is the sole edit and E imine geometry is retained; F owns GLY96.O at 3.51 A, but halogen substitution does not establish conversion of packing against backbone oxygen into a hydrophobic contact.

item_048.one_line_why: Only F becomes Cl, preserving all rings and heteroatoms; F32 owns the 3.47 A hydrophobic contact with LEU100.CD1, supporting the tentative local hydrophobic-packing rationale.
